text:
The decay is a two‑body decay at rest.  
With \(c=1\),

\[
m_{\pi}=E_{\mu}+E_{\nu},\qquad 
\vec p_{\mu}=-\vec p_{\nu}=p .
\]

For the (essentially massless) neutrino \(E_{\nu}=p\).  
For the muon \(E_{\mu}=\sqrt{p^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}}\).

Thus  

\[
m_{\pi}= \sqrt{p^{2}+m_{\mu}^{2}}+p
\]

\[
\Rightarrow p =\frac{m_{\pi}^{2}-m_{\mu}^{2}}{2m_{\pi}} .
\]

Insert the given masses (in MeV):

\[
m_{\pi}=139.6,\qquad m_{\mu}=105.7
\]

\[
p =\frac{139.6^{2}-105.7^{2}}{2\times139.6}
   =\frac{8315.7}{279.2}\approx 29.8\ \text{MeV}.
\]

Hence  

* Neutrino kinetic energy \(K_{\nu}=E_{\nu}=p\approx 29.8\ \text{MeV}\).

* Muon total energy \(E_{\mu}=m_{\pi}-p\approx 139.6-29.8=109.8\ \text{MeV}\).

  Muon kinetic energy  

\[
K_{\mu}=E_{\mu}-m_{\mu}=109.8-105.7\approx 4.1\ \text{MeV}.
\]

These values correspond to option (A).

**Answer: A**
